I've finished verifying A's round 7, and the round **fails**. One check fails outright, and the drift bug the round was meant to fix (CΓÇæR6ΓÇæ02) is still open. Everything else in scope passes, and the premium sign-in is not bypassed. The report is `tmp/studio-real-loop/c-round-7.md`, with `c-round-7.json` and evidence under `c-round-7/` for B. I changed no app source and made no commits.

**Failed**
- **RF7-3 (new bug CΓÇæR7ΓÇæ01, Medium):** the rule is that 300 ms after each of the first 3 loop wraps, the video must be between 2.29 and 2.31 s. In the first run it was at 2.244 s, 56 ms late. That run was valid (no stalls, no app slow frames, CPU about 15 %), so it can't be replaced. The later setup runs were also late, at 2.286 and 2.280 s; round 6 had none like this. Pressing Play after the loops does work: it starts within 10 ms of the scheduled time and stays within the drift limits.

**Still open**
- **CΓÇæR6ΓÇæ02 (drift bug):** the drift check (RF7-2) and the per-frame check (RF7-P1) pass as written: 3 of 3 runs pass in each layout, and forced layout is 0. But one run I had to discard because the machine was busy still showed the roundΓÇæ6 pattern: two slow frames of 49 ms and 61 ms blamed on `ArrangementContext`, at the same moments the video slipped. Forced layout was already 0 before A's fix, so that check can't confirm the cause. A has two leftovers B could target next (the library preview time that re-renders every frame, and the re-render after Play). The Tech Lead run on a quiet Chrome (VP9 and H.264) is still the evidence that's needed.
- **CΓÇæR7ΓÇæ02 (Low):** the ruler-label cases the task named are within 1 px. At a few other zoom levels I tested, the overflow reaches 1.41ΓÇô1.47 px.

**Passed**
- **Play responsiveness (RF7-P2):** the render-count test shows clips, overview bars, library rows and ruler ticks don't re-render on Play. In the browser, none of 5 Play clicks produced a slow frame, so the "Γëñ 16 ms" rule is met only because there was nothing to measure. The clicks themselves took 7.3 ms (median) to handle.
- **Ruler labels (S2):** the named overflow cases and the 4ΓÇæminute and 20ΓÇæminute Fit checks pass at 1280├ù720 and 1440├ù900.
- **Volume slider as a gesture (S3):**
  - A second pointer can't move a clip while the slider is held.
  - Releasing the slider writes exactly one Volume entry.
  - Blur or cancel mid-drag restores the old value with no entry.
  - Arrow keys on the slider are refused during a clip drag.
- **Docs and gates:**
  - Docs 015/016 make no unverified PASS claims.
  - Types, 779 tests and the build pass.
  - The protected files and `Header.tsx` are unchanged.
  - The source didn't change while I was verifying.
- **Related behaviour:**
  - Gesture conflicts, navigation while playing and per-frame screen updates have no regressions.
  - Play from position, Play after reaching the end (with a real Space key) and the loop wrap all work.
- **Full user flow:** search ΓåÆ stems ΓåÆ preview ΓåÆ drag a stem onto a track ΓåÆ drop video ΓåÆ play ΓåÆ export. The export is a 26.000 s, 24-bit, 48 kHz WAV: the gap is silent and the bass starts at 10.000125 s, the same as round 6.
- **Anonymous access:** opening `/studio-lab` directly in a fresh browser with no credentials loads only the 2 demo MP3s. After play and export there are no studio-token, recording, download or R2 requests. The token endpoint returns 401 when anonymous. A fake token gets a 500 and no token, but the backend on 5199 is down, so that path is only partly tested.

**Not tested this round:** the 21 older roundΓÇæ6 checks deferred to the milestone regression, real-mouse and multi-touch checks, and quiet-machine Chrome runs. These, plus the open items from the pre-push review and publication checkpoint, are listed in ┬º10 of the report.

The first C session ran out of usage partway through. I reused its measurements, discarded two of its result files whose origin I couldn't trace, and re-ran the Play-from-position and slider-keyboard checks.
